yarn-troppo.meaning: All the steps survive, but "medications you gave up on ages ago" narrows "medications you no longer use", and "Worth asking next time you're in for a script." adds advice the original doesn't give. The other asides ("Simple as that.", "Done and dusted.") are colour.
yarn-troppo.sense: "chock-a-block", "get shot of", "have a squiz", "nobody'd want a bar of" all fit, but the opener "Strewth, where do I start?" uses an exclamation of surprise where nothing surprising has happened, and "Here's the kicker" frames a safety fact as a twist.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Some natural lines ("Have a word with your local cops", "Then bin the packaging too."), but stock phrases are bolted on: "Strewth, where do I start?", "the whole box and dice", "Done and dusted.", "Not on the list, not down the loo."
yarn-troppo.register: Far heavier than a level 2 public-health page: an exclamation opener, tag lines after most sections ("That one's no joke.", "That's what they're there for."), "the dunny", "your local cops". No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The original is plain safety guidance; the quips make it breezy in places, worst at the fentanyl warning: "Here's the kicker: even after a patch has been used".
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads easily, though the stream of tags ("Simple as that.", "Done and dusted.") adds bumps at the end of steps.
yarn-troppo.variety: Plenty of different terms with none leaned on: "chock-a-block", "get shot of", "on the cards", "squiz", "loo", "dunny", "bin".
yarn-troppo.essence: Still the FDA disposal guide in shape, but its sober public-service character is flattened into a chatty bit: "Strewth, where do I start?"

dinkum-3.meaning: Every step and condition survives: "Pop them in the post in a prepaid drug mail-back envelope", "don't flush your medicine unless it's on the flush list", "Then bin the packaging."
dinkum-3.sense: "chockers", "your best bet", "Have a squiz", "chemists", "bar the ones on the FDA flush list" all carry the original's sense.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian health page written in plain speech: "Some chemists'll even give you one for nothing.", "an empty tin".
dinkum-3.register: A light touch at level 2: "chockers", "squiz", "dunny" once, otherwise plain Australian English. No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Stays practical and serious: "Some medicines could do real harm to someone else".
dinkum-3.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "If neither of those works for you, here's what to do:"
dinkum-3.variety: Varied verbs and terms for disposal: "get rid of", "toss it out", "Pop them in the post", "bin the packaging".
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the FDA guide, steps and warnings intact.

engine.meaning: The original nearly word for word, so every point survives: "Check with your local law enforcement officials to find a location near you".
engine.authenticity: US forms left in beside the swaps: "household trash", "unrecognizable", "Mail the envelope using the U.S. Postal Service", "retail pharmacies" next to "chemists". "heaps of the medicine remains" is a stiff join.
engine.register: Largely untranslated; a handful of words changed ("chemists", "dunny", "heaps"), well under a level 2 light touch.
engine.tone: The original's plain tone kept whole: "Remember, don’t flush your medicine unless it is on the flush list."
engine.flow: Keeps the original's slips ("To discard of your prescription", "Drop off them at a drug take-back location.") and adds "heaps of the medicine remains".
engine.variety: Too few terms to show range; nothing repeated beyond "rubbish".

unharnessed.meaning: Every step survives: "Scratch out all your personal details on the empty medicine packaging", "a fair bit of the medicine is still left in it".
unharnessed.sense: "chockers", "Chuck the container in the bin", "a fair bit", "rummaging through the bin" all fit.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural plain Australian ("Chuck the container in the bin at home.", "empty tin"), but it mixes "pharmacies" and "chemists" in one paragraph: "including chemists and online. Some pharmacies give them out for free."
unharnessed.register: A light level 2 touch: "chockers", "chuck", "a fair bit", otherwise plain. No swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Stays practical and serious: "Because some medicines could be especially harmful to other people".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth, but "get rid of" recurs so often it drags: "the best way to get rid of", "To get rid of your prescription", "get rid of it at home", "get rid of medicines safely".
unharnessed.variety: "get rid of" stands in for nearly every "dispose of" and "discard", seven or so times through the text.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the FDA guide, steps and warnings intact.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every step survives, but it adds "ask your doctor or other health care professional, or your pharmacist" where the original names only a health care professional or pharmacist; harmless but new.
yarn-dinkum.sense: "chock-a-block", "offload", "bin it at home", "Have a squiz", "Chuck the container" all fit.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like plain Australian speech: "Some chemists give them out for free.", "Then bin the packaging."
yarn-dinkum.register: Light level 2 touch: "chock-a-block", "squiz", "dunny" once. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Stays practical and serious: "Because some medicines could be especially harmful to other people".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly: "If you can't do either of those, follow these guidelines:"
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "offload", "bin it", "Chuck", "squiz"; "heaps" and "chemists" are the usual picks.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the FDA guide, steps and warnings intact.
